answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with decaying reputation bonds: each identity stakes collateral that unlocks slowly, like a glacier releasing meltwater, so a new identity starts with near-zero trust and must earn it through verifiable work. Fabricating a thousand fake agents means locking a thousand stakes, and slashing rules burn the bond of any identity caught lying. A ferrous backbone of on-chain attestations links each action to its stake, and market makers price trust by bond age, the way saffron is priced by labor — faking reputation becomes more expensive than earning it honestly.
